\[
I_{\text{out}}(x) = \frac{\sum_{i} k\!\left(\frac{i - u}{f}\right) I(i)}{\sum_{i} k\!\left(\frac{i - u}{f}\right)},
\qquad
u = \left(x + \tfrac{1}{2}\right) s - \tfrac{1}{2},
\qquad
f = \max(s, 1)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Source value, premultiplied by alpha
- \(I_{\text{out}}\): Output value, before it is divided by alpha
- \(x\): Output pixel index
- \(i\): Source pixel index
- \(u\): Source position of the center of output pixel x, in pixel-center units
- \(s\): Source size divided by output size
- \(f\): Kernel stretch, 1 when enlarging and s when shrinking
- \(k\): The kernel of the chosen method

Pixel i covers the interval from i to i + 1, so its center is i + 1/2. The center of output pixel x falls at the source position u. The kernel k weights the source pixels near u, and dividing by the sum makes the weights add up to 1. When shrinking, the kernel is f times wider, so each new pixel also averages the pixels it covers. That prevents aliasing. The same step runs along rows, then along columns.
